 UMMC Expands Free Dengue Vaccination And Health Screening For Children In Klang Valley
 By CodeBlue | 
 26 October 2026 
 UMMC’s Program Saringan Anemia dan Pencegahan Denggi brings free screening and vaccination services closer to families across the Klang Valley.
 Between May and October 2026, more than 3,600 children took part in the programme, with 60 to 70 per cent opting to receive dengue vaccination. Photo courtesy of UMMC. 
 KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Universiti Malaya Medical Centre (UMMC) is expanding access to free screening for anaemia (low blood count) and optional dengue vaccination for eligible children aged 7 to under 12 through additional weekend community drives across the Klang Valley.
 This programme screens children for anaemia, a condition that frequently goes undetected. Affected children may tire quickly, find it hard to concentrate in school, appear pale, or seem to lack energy. Left unrecognised, anaemia can impair learning, growth and development.
 Children with anaemia are also more vulnerable to severe illness if they contract dengue, making early detection doubly important in dengue-endemic settings.
 The expansion builds on encouraging turnout at earlier programmes across the Klang Valley and aims to reach more families amid Malaysia’s growing dengue burden. By October 14, 2026, more than 76,000 dengue cases have been reported nationwide.
 Dengue-related deaths also nearly doubled by early September 2026, with 62 deaths reported, compared with 32 during the same period in 2025.
 An international review also found that children with dengue were two times more likely to develop severe dengue compared with adults.
 For children and their families, dengue can mean hospitalisation, missed school time, and time away from everyday activities. Fatigue can persist for several weeks after recovery, while parents may need time off work to provide care.
 Between May and October 2026, more than 3,600 children took part in the programme, with 60 to 70 per cent opting to receive dengue vaccination. Community sessions were held in Petaling Jaya, Ampang, Kepong, Subang and Shah Alam.
 “The response so far has been encouraging, and we want more families to be able to participate. By holding more sessions close to home and at weekends, we hope to make it easier for parents to have their children screened and discuss dengue prevention with our medical team,” said Prof Dr Rafdzah Ahmad Zaki, public health medicine specialist at UMMC.
 Selected community sessions will also feature clowns, balloons, supadoopa, and goodie bags. Parents and guardians can register their eligible children for an upcoming session or visit UMMC for weekday walk-ins, available from Tuesday to Friday, until October 30, 2026.
 Families are also encouraged to remove mosquito breeding sites, prevent mosquito bites, and seek medical advice promptly if dengue is suspected.
 Here is the list of upcoming community sessions:
 November 1, 2026, Masjid Subang Perdana (9.00am to 3.00pm), registration link .
 November 14, 2026, PPR Pinggiran Bukit Jalil (9.00am to 3.00pm), registration link .
 November 22, 2026, Apartment Idaman Damansara Damai PJU 10/1 (9.00am to 3.00pm), registration link .
 November 28, 2026, PPR Lembah Subang 2 (9.00am to 3.00pm), registration link .
 Parents and guardians can register their children using the relevant links above or walk in on the day of the event.
